hook: 7 conversion killers hiding on your website right now.
direction: Carousel, one killer + fix per slide: slow load, buried CTA (or buried "Plan Your Visit"), insider jargon, no proof, mobile neglect, generic stock imagery, forms that interrogate. Examples alternate between business and church/nonprofit contexts.

facebook.text:
7 conversion killers hiding on your website right now.

You worked hard to get people there. Don't lose them to a fixable problem.

1. Slow load — visitors leave in 3 seconds
2. Buried CTA — if they have to hunt for "Give" or "Plan Your Visit," most won't
3. Insider jargon — your acronyms mean nothing to a first-timer
4. No proof — no testimonials, no stories, no reason to trust you
5. Mobile neglect — over half your traffic is on a phone
6. Generic stock photos — nobody believes the handshake photo
7. Forms that interrogate — asking for too much kills follow-through

One or two of these are probably costing you right now. Fix the worst one this week.

cover.title: 7 Conversion Killers
cover.subtitle: Hiding on your website right now — one problem, one fix.

slides.title: 1. Slow Load
slides.body: Business: A 3-second delay cuts conversions in half. Compress images, cut bloated plugins. Church: Visitors checking service times on Sunday morning won't wait.

slides.title: 2. Buried CTA
slides.body: Business: "Contact Us" shouldn't require scrolling. Put the next step above the fold. Church: "Plan Your Visit" belongs at the top — not buried in a dropdown.

slides.title: 3. Insider Jargon
slides.body: Church: "Join us for Midweek Equipping" means nothing to a newcomer. Say what it is. Business: Drop the industry acronyms. Write for the person who just found you.

slides.title: 4. No Proof
slides.body: Business: No reviews, no case studies — no reason to trust you. Add one real testimonial. Nonprofit: A single donor story does more than a page of statistics.

slides.title: 5. Mobile Neglect
slides.body: Church: Most people check your site on a phone before they visit. Test it. Business: Tiny buttons and pinch-to-zoom forms lose customers before they start.

slides.title: 6. Generic Stock Photos
slides.body: Business: The handshake photo signals nothing real. Use actual photos of your work. Church: Real people from your congregation beat a smiling stock family every time.

slides.title: 7. Forms That Interrogate
slides.body: Nonprofit: Asking for phone, address, and employer before someone can volunteer? Cut it. Business: Name and email is enough to start. Ask for more later.

end.title: Fix One This Week
end.subtitle: You don't need more traffic. You need to stop losing what you have.
